title: Health Systems
subtitle: Post-viral illness and brainstem attractor dynamics
description: Investigates ME/CFS and post-viral syndromes as emergent attractor states — conditions where the nervous system settles into a dysfunctional stable basin following viral insult. We model the population epidemiology of ME/CFS conversion, the role of brainstem-HPA axis dysregulation, and intervention pathways that might shift the system toward recovery basins.
research_questions: What combination of pre-existing risk factors most reliably predicts ME/CFS conversion post-infection?
Can brainstem mechanical load (Chiari, CCI) be modelled as a structural attractor modifier?
How do social and environmental stressors interact with immune function to shape post-viral trajectory?
Does a bistable regulatory-capture model (sustained cortical/limbic override of the respiratory pacemaker) account for why the illness state outlasts its trigger?
ai_use: AI assists in interpreting multi-run simulation outputs, identifying non-linear risk interactions, and connecting simulation findings to published epidemiological literature.

title: Literary Systems
subtitle: Narrative structure as a feedback system
description: Applies cross-system synthesis to the craft and impact of writing. Narrative is modelled as a feedback network: reader clarity, tension, and engagement are interdependent nodes. We develop a Reader-First framework that helps authors understand how structural choices propagate through the reading experience — and where interventions have the highest leverage.
research_questions: How do reinforcing and balancing feedback loops manifest in effective narrative structure?
Can system-level analysis predict reader drop-off, confusion, or emotional disengagement?
What is the optimal tension-clarity trade-off for different reader objectives?
ai_use: AI assists in generating structural critiques of narrative drafts, suggesting rebalancing interventions, and mapping text passages to feedback graph nodes.

title: Global Futurism
subtitle: Civilisational tipping points and macro-scale attractors
description: Models the macro-dynamics of civilisation as a complex adaptive system — one with multiple potential attractor basins ranging from stable cooperation to system-wide collapse. We investigate how inequality, technological acceleration, climate stress, and social infrastructure interact to push societies toward or away from tipping points.
research_questions: Which combinations of stressors most reliably push civilisational systems past bifurcation thresholds?
Do socio-economic tipping points follow the same attractor geometry as physical systems?
What interventions at the system level have the highest leverage for stabilising cooperative attractor states?
ai_use: AI assists in scenario generation, cross-domain pattern recognition, and connecting simulation states to current geopolitical and economic indicators.

title: Writing With AI
subtitle: Designing AI-assisted systems that scaffold expert writing practice
description: Investigates expert long-form writing as a complex cognitive system, and asks what a software environment looks like when it is built around the structure of that process — clarity, tension, structural revision, voice — rather than around the easier-to-automate task of generating text. This program produced ISRD Writing Studio (formerly Systemic Writer), an AI-assisted writing environment built as a design experiment: software as both output and evidence that the underlying model of the writing process holds up under real-world use.
research_questions: What is the cognitive structure of expert long-form writing, and where are its highest-leverage intervention points?
Can an AI-assisted environment scaffold that structure — preserving human judgment at every consequential decision — without collapsing into pure text generation?
Does a production system built on this model function as evidence that the underlying theory of the writing process is accurate?
ai_use: AI is the core process facilitator under study — not a novelty feature. The program investigates how language models can be structured to support, rather than replace, expert judgment throughout the writing process.

title: Reader-First Writing System
subtitle: The cognitive and systems basis for reader-centered writing
description: The cognitive and systems basis for reader-centered instructional writing: designing documents that transfer understanding. The program treats the reader as the system being designed for, and builds a method for long-form writing around the reader's evolving state, expectations and motivation.
